claim: HM Treasury consulted in September 2025 on A Streamlined Approach to Payment Systems Regulation.
The PSR's current legal basis is Part 5 of FSBRA 2013, and existing PSR directions including APP reimbursement continue until equivalent FCA rules replace them.
HMT's consultation response confirmed it will abolish the PSR and move its functions into the FCA, subject to primary legislation.
Functions moving to the FCA include those under the PSRs 2017, the Payment Card Interchange Fee Regulations 2015 and the Payment Accounts Regulations 2015 (including oversight of CASS).

A designation regime will be kept; appeals against specific directions would go to the High Court instead of the Competition Appeal Tribunal; transitional legislation would preserve PSR requirements including APP reimbursement.
The Financial Services and Markets Bill had its first reading in the House of Lords on 19 May 2026, with Lords second reading scheduled for 8 June 2026.
The Bill also covers FOS reform (10-year limit on complaints, adapted fair and reasonable test), SM&CR changes (removing the Certification Regime) and ring-fencing.
Lords committee stage sittings were held or scheduled for 22, 24 and 29 June and 1, 6 and 8 July 2026; payment-systems amendments were debated on 24 June.
The PSR will cease to exist as a separate body only on commencement, by commencement or saving regulations.
SD14 and SD15 (card acquiring), SD20 and SD21 (APP reimbursement) and General Direction 3 (open banking access) would move to the FCA; commercial VRP is not in this Bill.
Industry's working view is that firms will feel no impact from PSR consolidation before 2028.

PSR Annual Report 2025/26 (17 Aug 2026) says the Bill would abolish the PSR and transfer its functions to the FCA preserving its substance and scope; staff formally transferred to the FCA deliver PSR work under a service agreement.
The PSR board is chaired by Ashley Alder, the FCA Chair.
A trade article of 16 Jan 2026 says the PSR has since been merged into the FCA; this is legally inaccurate as of Oct 2026 because the Bill had not been enacted or commenced on the evidence found.

The Payments Forward Plan (26 Feb 2026) says PSR consolidation needs primary legislation when Parliamentary time allows, and the PSR is due to decide next steps on UK-EEA cross-border interchange in Q4 2026.
The BoE owns and operates RTGS, where eligible institutions hold reserves and settle in central bank money.
The BoE took over CHAPS operation from CHAPS Co in November 2017.
The BoE supervises payment systems recognised by HM Treasury, and on 22 Sep 2026 published a consultation on a fees regime for recognised payment systems and specified service providers.

RPIB is a senior industry advisory board chaired by the BoE (Victoria Cleland) that will oversee a new industry-led Delivery Company for future retail payments infrastructure; its consultation ran 25 Jun to 11 Sep 2026.
Pay.UK keeps operating FPS, Bacs and ICS while the RPIB work proceeds.
The PRA confirmed the £120,000 FSCS deposit limit after a March 2025 consultation.

The FCA is conduct regulator for PIs and EMIs (PS25/12 safeguarding, operational resilience scope), the access-to-cash regulator (PS24/8) and the future open banking regulator awaiting DUA Act powers.
The BoE, PRA and FCA jointly oversee designated critical third parties.
HMT designates payment systems and critical third parties, sets the Payments Forward Plan and is to lay the DUA Act open banking SI (planned Q4 2026).
OFSI, part of HM Treasury, implements and enforces UK financial sanctions: it publishes the consolidated list, issues general licences, takes breach reports and imposes monetary penalties.
OFSI published its Strategy 2026 to 2029 on 15 Apr 2026; the page was last updated 13 Oct 2026.

Pay.UK Limited is a company limited by guarantee (Company No. 10872449) that operates Bacs, owns and manages Direct Debit, and describes itself as the recognised operator and standards body for UK interbank retail payment systems.
On 17 Dec 2025 Pay.UK extended its Vocalink contracts for the central infrastructure of FPS, Bacs and ICS, giving continuity into the early 2030s.
OBL (formerly OBIE) is the Implementation Entity under the CMA Order; it maintains the Open Banking Standard and runs the Open Banking Directory, a dispute platform and monitoring for the Trustee.
The CMA said the open banking Roadmap was complete in January 2023; OBL reported passing 1 billion payments and 100 billion API calls (news item, 30 Jul 2026).

FCA letter of 19 Dec 2025: industry is to set up a body that could become the Future Entity, the primary UK API standard-setting body; OBL and the Smart Data Group were the candidates and the FCA expects to use DUA Act powers.
KPMG's independent assessment with an Industry Evaluation Panel (1 May 2026) scored OBL 63.88 and SDG 46 out of 76; no formal decision reported.

FSCS covers £120,000 per eligible person per authorised bank, building society or credit union for firms failing after 30 Nov 2025; temporary high balances up to £1.4m for six months; compensation within 7 working days; banks sharing a licence count as one.
FOS award limits from 1 Apr 2026 are £455,000 for acts or omissions on or after 1 Apr 2019 and £205,000 for earlier ones.
CHAPS runs 06:00 to 18:00 Monday to Friday excluding England and Wales bank holidays; customer payments must be submitted by 17:40.
CHAPS payments settle individually, gross, in RTGS on the day submitted and are irrevocable; there is no minimum or maximum value.
CHAPS has over 35 direct participants (including ClearBank and Fnality UK) and several thousand indirect ones; joining takes 12 to 18 months.

Direct participants need a reserves or settlement account, SFR participant status, a security and resilience attestation, compliance with the CHAPS Reference Manual and annual self-certification; the BoE is SFR designating authority for CHAPS.
SWIFT MIRS is the CHAPS third-site contingency.
Liquidity Saving Mechanism (since April 2013): urgent payments settle one by one, while matching cycles every few minutes settle offsetting non-urgent payments together, which stay legally gross.

RTGS account types: reserves accounts (SMF participants, remunerated at Bank Rate); settlement accounts for authorised non-bank PSPs (FCA non-objection, no reserves account or intraday liquidity); prefunding accounts (RCA, SCA, CFA); CREST settlement accounts (zero balance overnight).
Non-bank PSPs have had RTGS settlement account access since July 2017.
RT2, the renewed RTGS, was introduced in April 2025; RTGS is closed for settlement between 19:00 and 00:15.
The near-24x7 consultation ran 18 May to 10 Aug 2026 and proposes Sunday settlement (01:30 to 18:00) not before 2029, then 22x6 not before 2031, with 22x7 or 23.5x7 as long-term options.
The BoE Synchronisation Lab launched in May 2026 with 18 organisations.

Policy decision (24 Feb 2026): CHAPS settlement will open at 01:30 from September 2027, subject to confirmation with direct participants; sending in that window is optional and payment types are unrestricted.
CLS pay-ins and CCP margin calls are not expected to move; Notes Circulation Scheme settlement moves from 05:15 to 01:15.
CHAPS and RTGS migrated to ISO 20022 on 19 Jun 2023.

Since May 2025 purpose codes are mandatory for FI-to-FI and property payments and LEIs for FI-to-FI payments; from November 2027 purpose codes become mandatory for all CHAPS payments and LEIs for pacs.004 returns and pacs.009 COV.

Structured remittance will not be mandated from November 2026; removal of unstructured addresses is expected to move to November 2027 (subject to confirmation); usage guidelines are HVPS+ and CBPR+ with no version stated (page updated 27 Aug 2026).
CHAPS APP reimbursement has been in force since 7 Oct 2024, maximum £85,000 per claim for UK retail CHAPS payments, set by the PSR (PS24/5) and implemented by BoE CHAPS reimbursement rules.
CHAPS messages travel over SWIFT and settlement confirmation returns over SWIFT before the receiving bank is notified (2017 PFMI description; needs re-verification for RT2).
FPS is available day and night, 365 days per year; it was created in 2008; payments up to £1m with individual PSP limits varying.
Since 2018, non-bank FPS direct participants hold BoE settlement accounts.
FPS 2025 volume: 5.55bn transactions worth £4.84tn.
The £1m FPS scheme limit (up from £250,000) has been available since 10 Feb 2022.
FPS transaction types are Single Immediate Payment, Forward-Dated Payment, Standing Order (weekdays only, moved to next working day if needed) and Direct Corporate Access, each limited to £1m.

FPS settles deferred net in RTGS three times per business day; prefunding was introduced in September 2015 with direct settlement participants holding cash in collateralisation accounts at least equal to their net debit cap; RCA balances count toward reserves.
The 2018 timetable shows FPS settlement at 07:05, 13:05 and 17:05 (needs verification for 2026).

Directly Connected Settling Participants hold prefunded liquidity at the BoE; Net Sender Caps limit what a participant can owe others in each settlement cycle and are set by formula (Minimum Net Sender Cap and Peak Contingency Value).
Under an optional Pay.UK proposal (1 Jul 2026), participants would set their own Net Sender Caps, submitting quarterly plans, with no system change.
Execution time in law: PSRs 2017 reg 86 (payments to a payment account), reg 89 (value date and availability) and reg 94A (charges and interest for a delay under reg 86(2B)).

The Payment Services (Amendment) Regulations 2024 (in force 30 Oct 2024) let a payer's PSP delay an outbound payment to no later than end of D+4 if it has reasonable grounds to suspect fraud or dishonesty by end of D+1, informing the customer by end of D+1.
Bacs covers Direct Debit and Direct Credit; in 2025 it carried 6.86bn payments worth £6.05tn, including a record 5.0bn Direct Debits.
Bacs runs a three-day cycle with net settlement once per business day (09:30 in the 2018 timetable) and is prefunded.
ICS runs a two-day cycle with net settlement once a day (16:30 in the 2018 timetable).

Direct Debit Guarantee: advance notice of amount or date changes (normally 10 working days); full and immediate refund from the payer's bank or building society if an error is made; cancellation at any time via the bank.
The RPIB consultation will inform a blueprint that a Delivery Company will deliver, covering A2A at the point of sale and better cross-border payments; the NPA is not mentioned.
A response to the RPIB consultation is due between July and December 2026.
Visa has settled sterling net in RTGS since November 2013 in 24-hour cycles, with weekend cycles settling on the next business day; LINK uses the same pattern.
The 2018 timetable shows Visa settlement at 14:00 and LINK at 11:00.

Visa Core Rules (18 April 2026 edition) have sections on authorisation (7.3: routing, declines, response time limits), clearing (7.5), settlement (7.7, National Net Settlement Service 7.7.1), interchange (1.8) and disputes (11).

UK IFR caps consumer debit and prepaid interchange at 0.2% and consumer credit at 0.3%, in effect since 9 Dec 2015; since EU exit they apply only where merchant, acquirer and issuer are all in the UK, so UK-EU cross-border consumer transactions are uncapped.
The PSR is lead competent authority under the Payment Card Interchange Fee Regulations 2015.

On 15 Jan 2026 the High Court rejected the challenge by Visa, Mastercard and Revolut and upheld the PSR's power to cap cross-border interchange; UK-EEA CNP fees had risen to 1.15% (consumer debit) and 1.5% (consumer credit); cap level not yet set.
A price-cap consultation or implementation is expected in late 2026 or 2027.
The March 2025 scheme and processing fees final report found the market not working effectively; transparency-focused remedies were under consultation in 2026.
Under CCA 1974 s75 the card issuer is jointly and severally liable with the supplier for misrepresentation or breach on single items with a cash price above £100 and up to £30,000.

FCA PS24/8 (published 24 Jul 2024, in force 18 Sep 2024, under Part 8B FSMA 2000) requires HMT-designated firms and coordination bodies to assess local cash needs and provide extra services where there is a significant gap.
LINK (Link Scheme Holdings Ltd) describes itself as the UK's not-for-profit cash machine and access-to-cash network, governed by an independent board.
The FCA's access-to-cash post-implementation review findings are due in Q2 2027.

SD17 (made 10 Oct 2022 under FSBRA s54, in force 24 Oct 2022) requires directed PSPs to send and respond to CoP requests using Pay.UK rules; Group 1 (32 named PSPs) by 31 Oct 2023, Group 2 (FPS or CHAPS participants with an EISCD sort code, or building societies) by 31 Oct 2024.

Draft SD17a (CP26/2) would add Group 3 by 31 Dec 2026 and replace the original 1 Nov 2026 cessation date with a review within five years; exemptions include bulk payments, MT202 transfers and merchant acquiring.
CoP is an API-based peer-to-peer name check with no central infrastructure, supported by a participant directory; over 300 organisations use it and it runs more than 2 million checks a day.
Payer Name Verification extends CoP to Bacs Direct Debit set-up.
PS24/7 (3 Oct 2024) set the maximum FPS APP reimbursement at £85,000 per claim, down from £415,000, with a commitment to keep it under review; policy start 7 Oct 2024.

APP reimbursement: sending and receiving firms split costs 50:50, most victims are reimbursed within five business days, covering FPS and CHAPS payments between UK accounts, resting on FSMA 2023 (Royal Assent June 2023).

Consumer explainer: excess up to £100 (not for vulnerable customers); stop the clock up to 35 business days; claims within 13 months; gross negligence exception (not for vulnerable customers); cards, cash, cheques, unauthorised fraud and civil disputes excluded.

Independent evaluation (1 Jul 2026): FPS APP losses fell about 21% (about £73m a year) and the share reimbursed rose from 54% to 65%; formal consultation planned for December 2026; no change to the limit found as of Oct 2026.
The BPS claims management system winds down in Q3 2027, with an industry decision on its replacement due January to June 2026.
The CMA Retail Banking Market Investigation Order 2017 (made 2 Feb 2017 under s161 Enterprise Act 2002) binds the CMA9, names OBL as Implementation Entity and has not been revoked.
PSRs 2017 regs 68 to 70 (CBPII funds confirmation, PIS, AIS) and reg 100 with the SCA-RTS apply to open banking.
HMT's 21 Apr 2026 package proposes FCA open banking powers and moving payments and e-money regulation into FSMA.

DUA Act 2025 (c. 18) Part 1 Access to customer data and business data: ss 2 to 7 data regulations, ss 8 to 10 enforcement, ss 11 to 13 fees and levy, ss 14 to 17 FCA and financial services interfaces; commencement in s142.

PFP timeline: FCA consultation on interface rules Q3 2026; HMT DUA Act SI giving FCA oversight (including of the Future Entity) and paving the way to revoke the CMA Order Q4 2026; FCA policy statement Q1 2027.

Open Banking Standard v4.0 makes FAPI 1.0 Advanced Final mandatory (FAPI 1.0 Draft 2 deprecated by end of 2024), with ISO 20022-aligned fields for BoE CHAPS requirements from 1 May 2025; TDA approved 26 Jun 2024.
JROC was designing the post-CMA-Order framework, and OBL refers to JROC recommendations for the future entity.

UKPI began operating a commercial VRP scheme on 2 Jun 2026; Wave 1 covers regulated financial services, government, utilities and rail; participating banks held about 75% of current accounts; Wave 2 (e-commerce) needs a Treasury SI.
UKPI was set up in 2025 by 31 firms; in January 2026 the FCA and PSR said they would not open competition investigations into phase-one cVRP pricing; Wave 2 expected late 2026 or early 2027.
The PFP target was first live VRPs under the industry-led scheme in Q1 2026; the reported launch (2 Jun 2026) was later.

PS25/12 (7 Aug 2025) took effect 7 May 2026 for authorised PIs (except PIS-only or AIS-only), authorised EMIs, small EMIs and credit unions issuing e-money; small PIs may opt in; the post-repeal CASS-style regime has no timeline.

CASS 15 detail: internal and external reconciliations each reconciliation day; monthly safeguarding return (SUP 16.14A); resolution pack (CASS 10A) retrievable within 48 hours; annual safeguarding audit (SUP 3A) with exemption below £100,000; statutory trust deferred.

EMRs 2011: reg 13 small EMI registration; regs 20 to 24 safeguarding (two options); regs 33 to 34 distributors and agents; regs 39 to 46 issuance, redemption and no interest (reg 45); revocation under FSMA 2023 Sch 1 Pt 2 listed as not yet in force.
PSRs 2017: regs 13 to 16 small PI registration, reg 23 safeguarding, reg 34 agents, reg 105 access to bank accounts; text current to 11 Oct 2026.
PFP: HMT consultation on reforming assimilated payments law (PSRs and EMRs) Q2 2026, response Q4 2026, payments SI 2027 to 2028.
The BoE considered overnight safeguarding facilities for non-bank RTGS account holders in January to June 2026 (outcome unknown).
MLRs 2017: CDD (regs 27 to 32), EDD (33 to 36, PEPs reg 35), supervisors (reg 7, regs 46 to 52B), transfer of funds (Part 7), cryptoasset transfers (Part 7A).
S.I. 2026/621 inserts reg 34A and Sch 6 para 7(ga) into the MLRs, shown as not yet applied to the text.
DPA 2018 (c. 12) includes the UK GDPR chapter; text current to 12 Oct 2026.

Operational resilience (PS21/3, SYSC 15A): transition ended 31 Mar 2025, after which firms must stay within impact tolerances for each important business service in severe but plausible scenarios; scope includes banks, building societies, insurers, RIEs, enhanced SM&CR firms, PSRs and EMR firms.

CTP rules in force since 1 Jan 2025; the Critical Third Parties (Designation) Regulations 2026 designated AWS EMEA SARL, Google Cloud EMEA Limited, Microsoft Ireland Operations Ltd and Oracle Corporation UK Limited with oversight from 13 Jul 2026; designation is not authorisation.

BoE progress update (4 Mar 2026): no decision has been made; the design phase ends in 2026 with four workstreams (assessment, blueprint, experiments and PoCs, engagement); six design notes were published in 2025; a decision is to be announced later this year.
Digital Pound Lab Phase 1 participants were Fluxpay, LINK with Consult Hyperion, NOBO Finance with Applied Blockchain, and Yotra; Phase 2 runs to July 2026.
The BoE is testing RT2 synchronisation and experimenting with wholesale CBDC on a separate DLT.

The March 2026 digital pound page says a live system already settles the sterling cash leg of tokenised transactions using a tokenised form of central bank money; this sits uneasily with the July 2026 wholesale page.
The digital pound news list has nothing after March 2026 (page updated 2 Apr 2026).

Earliest issuance would be in the second half of the decade; users would hold wallets with private intermediaries, not BoE accounts; a holding limit high enough for day-to-day spending is not yet set; no programming of money by the BoE or government.
On 25 Jun 2026 the RPIB release repeated that no decision had been taken on a digital pound and conclusions would come later in the year.
Whether the BoE/HMT decision and blueprint were published between July and 15 Oct 2026 could not be checked.

Synchronisation uses an earmark-and-release model in RT2 coordinated by third-party synchronisation operators that need no RTGS account; interface formats aligned to ISO 20022 where possible; builds on Project Meridian.
The BoE is committed to launching a live synchronisation service in 2028.
DSS participants may settle the cash leg using qualifying sterling or non-sterling stablecoins.
Cash-settlement options for the DIGIT digital gilt pilot are still being identified.
PFP stablecoin timeline: FCA issuance rules policy statement Q2 to Q3 2026, BoE systemic stablecoin final rules by end-2026, FCA crypto regime live October 2027.
The New Payments Architecture label does not appear in any 2025 or 2026 primary source opened; superseded or historical status needs verification.
FPS message format was not verified in the sources opened (widely reported as ISO 8583-based, not verified).

The FSM Bill 2026 completed its House of Lords stages (third reading 15 Sep 2026) and had its Commons first reading on 15 Sep 2026; Commons second reading not yet scheduled and no Royal Assent as of 15 Oct 2026 (added after independent fact-check).
The Board of Governors is a federal agency with seven governors on staggered 14-year terms, nominated by the President and confirmed by the Senate; it oversees Reserve Bank operations.
The 12 Reserve Banks (24 branches) distribute currency, operate electronic payment systems, clear checks, act as the Treasury's bank and examine banks.

The Board is the supervisory agency for TCH (operator of CHIPS) and CLS Bank International, two of eight FSOC-designated systemically important FMUs; the others (CME, DTC, FICC, ICE Clear Credit, NSCC, Options Clearing Corp) are supervised by the CFTC or SEC.

Account Access Guidelines published and implemented 19 Aug 2022 (87 FR 51099): legal eligibility under the Federal Reserve Act plus six risk principles; Tier 1 federally insured, Tier 2 non-insured but federally supervised by statute, Tier 3 all others (strictest review); decisions case by case.

The May 2026 Payment Accounts proposal (91 FR 30627) would let any already legally eligible institution request a Payment Account regardless of tier, with no interest, a Closing Balance Limit capped at $1 billion, no intraday credit, no discount window and no EBA participation.

Payment Account services would be Fedwire Funds, FedNow, NSS and Fedwire Securities (free-of-payment only); FedACH deliberately excluded for credit risk; holders cannot act as correspondent or respondent under Operating Circular 1.
Review timelines would be 90 days for Payment Account requests and 45 days for Tier 1 master account requests; comment deadline 27 Jul 2026 (closed); not finalized as of capture.

The proposal does not expand legal eligibility (expected applicants mostly non-federally insured depository institutions); the Board urged Reserve Banks to pause Tier 2 and Tier 3 decisions until it concludes, expected by 31 Dec 2026.

EO Integrating Financial Technology Innovation into Regulatory Frameworks (19 May 2026): Section 4 asks the Fed to evaluate account and service access for uninsured depository institutions, nonbanks (including digital asset firms) and direct real-time payment network participants, report due in 120 days; Section 3 asks CFPB, SEC, NCUA, CFTC, FDIC, OCC to review rules within 90 days.

FDIC is an independent agency (1933) insuring deposits at more than 4,000 institutions up to $250,000 per depositor, per insured bank, per ownership category; it directly supervises over 2,700 banks and savings associations and is primary federal regulator of state-chartered non-member banks.
FDIC resolves failures, usually by selling deposits and loans to an assuming bank, and is funded by bank assessments rather than congressional appropriations.
NCUA is an independent federal agency created in 1970 that charters and regulates federal credit unions and insures deposits via the Share Insurance Fund up to $250,000.
OCC, FRB, FDIC and NCUA each enforce Regulation II for their institutions, and the FTC for others.

FinCEN's mission is to safeguard the financial system from illicit activity and counter money laundering and terrorist financing through collection, analysis and dissemination of financial intelligence.

All US persons must comply with OFAC sanctions; SDN-listed persons are blocked and property within US jurisdiction must be frozen; entities 50% or more owned in aggregate by blocked persons are blocked; blocked property must be reported within 10 business days; voluntary self-disclosure is mitigating.

Acting Director Russell Vought concluded he could not request Fed funds while Fed interest expenses exceed income and in November 2025 said he would not request FY2026 funding; 22 states sued in December 2025 (D. Or.).

Judge Ann Aiken (reported 25 Sept 2026) held combined earnings means Fed revenue before expenses, vacated the funding decisions as contrary to law and a separation-of-powers violation, and ordered funding restored; appeal status unknown.

Vought requested $145 million for Q2 FY2026 and $75.8 million for Q3 FY2026 after $0 in Q3 FY2025, citing a D.D.C. preliminary injunction (Judge Amy Berman Jackson); on 31 Mar 2026 the CFPB moved to stay or modify that injunction with a Workforce Reduction Plan.
The One Big Beautiful Bill (2025) cut the CFPB funding cap from 12% to 6.5% of the Fed's 2009 operating expenses (inflation adjusted).

CFPB agenda (published July 2026): Section 1033 reconsideration NPRM (July 2026), larger participant revisions incl. international money transfers (Sept 2026), Reg E remittance disclosures final rule (Nov 2026), prepaid pre-rule (Nov 2026); planned, not adopted.
Section 1071 small business data reconsideration and ECOA/Reg B changes were issued 1 May 2026, effective July 2026 (deregulatory).
The CFPB overdraft final rule was issued 12 Dec 2024 (89 FR 106768), stated effective 1 Oct 2025; page last modified 2 Jul 2025 shows no CRA notice; its 2025 fate needs verification.
The CFPB digital payment apps larger participant rule was issued 21 Nov 2024 (89 FR 99582), effective 9 Jan 2025; CRA disapproval widely reported but not confirmed from an opened primary source.
The CSBS MTMA was enacted in full or in part in 31 states as of April 2026; Maryland adopted by regulation (COMAR 09.03.14); 2026 bills pending in Alaska, Louisiana, Maryland, Michigan, Oklahoma.

Fedwire Funds is an RTGS for credit transfers, typically large and time-sensitive; transfers are immediate, final and irrevocable once processed; participants are depository institutions and certain others holding a Reserve Bank account.

Fedwire business day runs 21:00 ET previous calendar day to 19:00 ET Monday to Friday excluding holidays; third-party transfer deadline 18:45 ET; only participant figure on the page is about 7,300 (2008).

Fedwire ISO 20022 went live 14 Jul 2025 after postponement of the original 10 Mar 2025 date; FAIM was the former proprietary format; FedLine Direct users can retrieve only ISO 20022 messages after cutover; processing speed unchanged; specifications on MyStandards.
Fedwire ISO 20022 go-live was confirmed on 18 Jun 2025.

Post-migration Fedwire materials reference camt.056, camt.029, pacs.004, camt.110/camt.111 and pain.014; duplicate checks extended to pacs.004 and camt.111 (Sept 2025 release); pacs.008/pacs.009 not named on pages opened.

The Board decided to expand Fedwire Funds to 22x6 (Sunday to Friday including weekday holidays) and NSS to 21.5x6, Saturdays excluded, Fedwire Securities not expanded, implementation 2028 or 2029; 22x7x365 only considered at least two years later via a new proposal.

Reg J subpart B incorporates UCC 4A as federal law for Fedwire, preempting inconsistent state law; Reserve Bank credit to the receiving bank is final and irrevocable when made and constitutes final settlement.

Fedwire transfers to or from consumer accounts are generally outside EFTA/Reg E, but EFTA s919 remittance rules prevail on conflict; s210.25(e) says messaging standards including ISO 20022 confer no legal status.

FedNow (production since 20 Jul 2023) processes 24x7x365 including weekends and holidays for US depository institutions, with optional receive-only participation, LMTs and optional request for payment in the first release.
FedNow uses ISO 20022, gives recipients full immediate access to funds, with baseline use cases A2A transfers and bill pay.

FedNow clears and settles in real time in Reserve Bank master accounts with no prefunding required; institutions may designate a correspondent; cycle date generally 19:00 to 19:00 ET aligned with Fedwire close.
FedNow LMTs can move funds between a master account and the joint account backing a private instant payment service (RTP context); LMT-only participation allowed.

Reg J subpart C: Reserve Bank credit to the receiving bank is final and irrevocable when made; the beneficiary's bank must credit immediately after acceptance; with reasonable cause (sanctions, suspected fraud) it may notify its Reserve Bank it needs more time.
Under Reg J subpart C, EFTA prevails on conflict, ACH is excluded, senders have no overdraft right and there are 60 calendar days to report unauthorized or erroneous orders.

On 24 Jun 2025 the FedNow network limit rose from $500,000 to $1 million with new account activity thresholds; about 1,400 participants then, over 95% community banks and credit unions; FedLine reaches 9,000+ institutions.

Effective 12 Nov 2025 the FedNow customer credit transfer and return network limit rose from $1 million to $10 million and the LMT limit from $2.5 million to $10 million; participants may set lower limits.
FedNow 2026 Q2: 4,997,811 settled payments (+83.2% y/y) worth $274,663,803,964 (+1.3% y/y), average $54,957, average daily volume 54,921.

FedNow has more than 1,800 banks and credit unions (up from over 1,600 in January 2026), including seven of the 10 largest US banks; 2025: 8.4 million transactions over $853.4 billion; Q1 2026: 2.7 million transactions, $271.3 billion.
Digital Transactions says the limit rose to $1M in March 2025, conflicting with the Fed's 24 Jun 2025 press release (March likely the announcement).

RTP runs 24/7, settlement is final and irrevocable, senders cannot revoke or recall, a separate message requests return of funds, and receivers must make funds available immediately subject to limited exceptions.

RTP is credit push only with request-for-payment messaging and a $10 million limit; open to any insured depository institution plus uninsured US branches and agencies of foreign banks, directly or via service provider; single price for all.
TCH is examined annually under the FFIEC Significant Service Provider program; RTP shares infrastructure with CHIPS; TCH claims 98% of US instant payments cleared and settled on RTP in 2025.
RTP had over 1,378 participants as of Sept 2026; 1.8 billion+ transactions and $3.6 trillion+ since 2017; Q3 2026: 150 million transactions worth $621 billion.
RTP daily average value is stated as $6.9 billion in the page body but over $4B daily in the page meta (internal inconsistency).

RTP settles through ledger positions backed by funds in the RTP Prefunded Balance Account at FRBNY, jointly owned by a subset of participants with TCH as agent; a Board order effective 7 Jun 2023 pays interest on these balances like master accounts, passed back per funding share.
The RTP limit rose from $1 million to $10 million effective 9 Feb 2025 (announced 4 Dec 2024).
TCH says RTP is owned by the world's largest commercial banks; the owner-bank page shows 21 logos (names inferred from logo files).

CHIPS: more than $2 trillion average daily value, 630,000+ transactions per business day, 43 direct participant banks, 21-hour processing window, continuous intraday settlement with a liquidity-saving mechanism, about 95% of payments final in seconds; ISO 20022 on an annual maintenance cycle.
TCH states CHIPS is not an end-of-day settlement system.
CHIPS prefunding mechanics (prefunded balances at FRBNY funded by Fedwire with end-of-day final funding) were not confirmed in opened TCH pages.

FedACH Same Day windows (deposit / target distribution / settlement, ET): 10:30 / 12:00 / 13:00; 14:45 / 16:00 / 17:00; 16:45 / 17:30 / 18:00; next-day items settle 08:30 ET; target distribution times carry no Reserve Bank liability.
Same Day ACH limit is $1 million per payment effective 18 Mar 2022; same-day processing was first enabled by a May 2015 rules change; ACH Rules, not FedACH, set limits and availability.

Nacha fraud monitoring Phase 1 (20 Mar 2026) covers all ODFIs plus large originators and RDFIs by 2023 volume; Phase 2 (19 Jun 2026) all others; requires risk-based processes for unauthorized and False Pretenses entries, reviewed annually; creates no duty to prevent and does not change UCC 4A liability.

False Pretenses means misrepresenting identity, association or authority, or account ownership (BEC, vendor or payroll impersonation), not poor-quality goods scams; the rules expand the earlier WEB debit and Micro-Entry fraud detection rule.
ACH returns within 2 banking days: R01, R02, R03, R04, R16, R29; within 60 calendar days (extended): R05, R07, R10, R11.
Reserve Banks clear checks.

Reg CC 229.10: cash deposited in person available next business day; electronic payments no later than the business day after receipt; certain official checks next business day if deposited in person; other checks the lesser of $275 or aggregate deposits.

Reg II requires fees reasonable and proportional to cost, offers a fraud-prevention adjustment, exempts small issuers, government programs and reloadable general-use prepaid, and bars restricting debit to fewer than two unaffiliated networks or inhibiting merchant routing.
The Fed's Reg II page lists the 25 Oct 2023 proposal to lower the cap without saying it was finalized.

Corner Post (D.N.D.): 6 Aug 2025 summary judgment vacated the fee standard but stayed vacatur pending appeal; 27 Oct 2025 amended judgment limited vacatur to 235.3(b); Eighth Circuit argued 13 May 2026, no decision as of 20 Sept 2026.
Linney's Pizza (E.D. Ky.) upheld Reg II on 15 Sept 2025, with Sixth Circuit argument set for 22 Oct 2026; Board revised exempt issuer lists 27 May 2026; CNP two-network routing effective 1 Jul 2023.
The 2023 proposal would set 14.4 cents base, 4.0 bps and a 1.3-cent fraud adjustment; comments closed 12 May 2024; no final rule or withdrawal found as of 20 Sept 2026.

The Credit Card Competition Act was reintroduced in January 2026 by Sens. Durbin and Marshall with Trump endorsement; attempts to attach it to the GENIUS Act (2025) and the ROAD to Housing Act (March 2026) failed; no floor vote.

Reg Z 1026.12(b) caps cardholder liability for unauthorized use at the lesser of $50 or the amount obtained before notice; 1026.12(c) lets cardholders assert merchant claims and defenses, generally for purchases over $50 in the home state or within 100 miles.

Reg Z 1026.13: billing error notice within 60 days of the first statement showing the error; acknowledge within 30 days; resolve within two complete billing cycles and no later than 90 days; no collection or adverse reporting meanwhile.

Reg E 1005.6: $50 liability if a lost or stolen device is reported within 2 business days, up to $500 otherwise; unauthorized transfers on a statement must be reported within 60 days to avoid liability for later transfers.

Visa Core Rules (18 Apr 2026) contain Dispute Conditions 10.1 EMV Liability Shift Counterfeit Fraud (11.7.2) and 10.2 EMV Liability Shift Non-Counterfeit Fraud (11.7.3), Table 1-12 EMV Liability Shift Participation and Dispute Category 13 consumer disputes (11.10); rule text not extracted.

Reg E 1005.11: notice within 60 days of statement; investigate within 10 business days, extendable to 45 calendar days with provisional credit; 90 days for out-of-state, POS debit and new-account transfers; 20 business days for new accounts.

Reg E 1005.30: remittance transfers are electronic transfers requested by a US consumer to a foreign recipient via a provider; transfers of $15 or less excluded; 500 or fewer transfers a year is not normal course of business; providers exceeding 500 generally have up to six months to comply.
Reg E 1005.34: cancellation if requested within 30 minutes of payment (funds not yet picked up), with full refund including fees within 3 business days.

Reg E 1005.33: errors include wrong amount and late delivery; notice within 180 days of disclosed availability date; provider determines within 90 days and reports within 3 business days; remedies refund or resend at no cost.

UCC 4A-209: a non-beneficiary receiving bank accepts by executing the order; the beneficiary's bank accepts at the earliest of paying or notifying the beneficiary, receiving full payment of the sender's order, or opening of the next funds-transfer business day if covered and not rejected.

Bank CIP (31 CFR 1020.220): obtain name, date of birth, address and identification number before account opening; risk-based verification to form a reasonable belief of identity; compare against terrorism-related lists; keep records 5 years after closure; reliance permitted.

CDD rule (31 CFR 1010.230): identify and verify beneficial owners of legal entity customers at account opening (each 25%+ owner up to four, plus one control person); exemptions include some POS credit up to $50,000; 5-year retention; no 2025/2026 amendment shown.
On 2 Mar 2025 Treasury suspended BOI enforcement against US citizens and domestic companies; the 26 Mar 2025 FinCEN interim final rule exempted domestic reporting companies.

FinCEN's 11 Aug 2026 final rule permanently exempts all US-created entities from BOI reporting; only foreign-law entities registered in a US state or tribal jurisdiction report; about 28,000 foreign entities estimated (about 13,000 filed by end-2025); effective date needs verification.
The 2016 bank CDD rule remains in effect and unaffected by the 2026 BOI final rule; FinCEN intends to modify it later without timeline.

Reg P (last amended 17 Sep 2018) requires initial (1016.4) and annual (1016.5) privacy notices, opt-out limits on disclosing NPI to nonaffiliated third parties (1016.7, 1016.10) and limits on sharing account numbers for marketing (1016.12).

FDIC standard maximum deposit insurance is at least $250,000 per depositor, per insured bank, per ownership category, covering checking, NOW, savings, MMDAs, CDs and official items; not stocks, bonds, mutual funds, annuities, insurance, safe deposit contents, Treasuries, munis or crypto assets.

FDIC Part 328 signage final rule (published 29 Jan 2026) is effective 2 Mar 2026 with compliance required by 1 Apr 2027; digital signs on homepage, login and account-opening start pages; ATMs on initial screen only.
The FDIC custodial account recordkeeping NPRM (RIN 3064-AG07, 2 Oct 2024) had comments extended to 16 Jan 2025 and is listed under Long-Term Actions with final rule To Be Determined; not withdrawn.

Section 1033 final rule published 22 Oct 2024; FDX recognized as standard setter 8 Jan 2025 (through Jan 2030); CFPB told court 23 May 2025 it views the rule as unlawful; stay granted after 29 Jul 2025; compliance tiers from 1 Apr 2026 suspended; enjoined, not formally vacated.
In Forcht Bank, N.A., et al. v. CFPB (E.D. Ky., No. 5:24-cv-00304), the court on 29 Oct 2025 enjoined the CFPB from enforcing the rule until it completes reconsideration.
Pre-injunction compliance date: Moore and Van Allen says prior orders extended it to 30 Jun 2026, while Open Banking Tracker says no 30 Jun 2026 deadline exists.
The 1033 reconsideration ANPR was published 22 Aug 2025 with comments to 21 Oct 2025, covering data provider fees, authorized representatives, privacy and security, and burden.
The 1 April 2026 compliance date arrived without being a binding enforcement trigger; the rule is paused, contested and being rewritten.
The CFPB submitted a Personal Financial Data Rights Reconsideration NPRM to OIRA (reported 6 Aug 2026); substance not public.

The 23 Jan 2025 EO sets a policy of prohibiting establishment, issuance, circulation and use of a CBDC in the US, prohibits agencies from acting to establish, issue or promote CBDCs except as required by law, terminates ongoing domestic CBDC plans and revokes EO 14067.

The EO defines CBDC as digital money denominated in the national unit of account that is a direct liability of the central bank, and creates the President's Working Group on Digital Asset Markets (report in 180 days).
The Federal Reserve CBDC page says it has made no decisions on whether to pursue a CBDC and references the January 2022 discussion paper; last updated 21 Jan 2022 (stale).

The 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act (H.R. 6644) passed the House 358-32 on 23 Jun 2026 and became law (press release 11 Jul 2026); it prohibits issuing a CBDC until 31 Dec 2030; public law number not given.
The Senate passed it 85-5 on 22 Jun 2026; the Board and Reserve Banks may not issue or create a CBDC, including any substantially similar digital asset issued directly or via an intermediary.
It became law without the President's signature by operation of the 10-day rule; The Block implies 10 Jul 2026, conflicting slightly with the committee's 11 Jul wording.
The Anti-CBDC Surveillance State Act (H.R. 1919 / S. 1124) is a bill, not law; the final FY2026 NDAA compromise text (10 Dec 2025) dropped the anti-CBDC provision.
TCH's RTP finality is stated by the network as final and irrevocable with no sender recall; RTP Operating Rules text was not opened.
Bulgaria adopted the euro on 1 Jan 2026, bringing euro-using EU Member States to 21; the Bulgarian National Bank joined the Eurosystem and its Governor joined the Governing Council.
The Bulgarian market joined all TARGET Services (T2, T2S, TIPS, ECMS) on 1 Jan 2026; euro settlement in TIPS had been possible for the Bulgarian market since 2024.
The SSM is the system of European banking supervision made up of the ECB and the national supervisory authorities of participating countries.

AMLA was legally established on 26 Jun 2024 with its seat in Frankfurt am Main; Chair Bruna Szego was appointed 21 Jan 2025 and took office 16 Feb 2025; Executive Board appointed 22 May 2025; about 120 staff by end-2025 and about 430 by end-2027.

AMLA will select 40 obliged entities for direct supervision during 2027 and start direct supervision during 2028; tasks include indirect supervision, FIU support and coordination including FIU.net, and technical standards.
AMLA seat history: call for host applications 28 Sep 2023, nine applicants by 10 Nov 2023, political agreement on Frankfurt 22 Feb 2024.

EBA payments mandates include the RTS on SCA and common secure communication (adopted, in OJ), guidelines on fraud reporting, and technical standards on the EBA register, authorisation, major incident reporting and complaints under PSD2.

EBA dated items: EBA/ECB payment fraud report 15 Dec 2025; MoU on non-bank PSP access to central bank payment systems 18 Dec 2025; 12 Feb 2026 opinion on end of the No-Action Letter transition ending 2 Mar 2026; SEPA Regulation NCA reporting decision 10 Apr 2026.
The ESAs jointly designated 19 critical ICT third-party providers under DORA on 18 Nov 2025; lead overseer per CTPP not stated.

The Commission proposed PSD3, PSR, FiDA and the digital euro on 28 Jun 2023, and on 8 Oct 2025 sent letters of formal notice to Member States not notifying transposition of the IPR's PSD2 and SFD amendments.
The EPC manages the five SEPA payment scheme rulebooks (SCT, SCT Inst, SDD Core, SDD B2B, OCT Inst) plus VOP, SEPA Request-to-Pay and SEPA Payment Account Access schemes.
EBA CLEARING offers EURO1, STEP2-T (SCT, SDD Core, SDD B2B), STEP2 CC (card clearing) and RT1, with VOP, R2P and FPAD services listed.
The digital euro pilot page cites staff from the ECB and 19 NCBs although the euro area has 21 NCBs; treated as stated.

T2 launched March 2023 replacing TARGET2, with components CLM (central liquidity management across TARGET Services) and RTGS (priorities, timed transactions, reservations, limits, pooling, optimisation).

T2 settles one by one, continuously, in central bank money with immediate finality and no upper or lower limit on payment value; used for monetary policy operations, interbank and commercial payments and other FMI settlement.
T2 opens Monday to Friday and is closed for euro on 1 Jan, Good Friday, Easter Monday, 1 May, 25 Dec and 26 Dec.
T2 direct participants are EEA financial institutions, including non-bank PSPs, holding an RTGS account; non-euro EU central banks may participate for euro settlement.
Danish krone was activated in T2 in April 2025; Sweden and Norway expressed interest; T2 shares ISO 20022 with T2S, TIPS and ECMS.

On 28 May 2026 the Eurosystem published a T2 hours roadmap (after a June 2025 consultation with 125 entities from 19 countries) starting with a short weekend and holiday liquidity-transfer window (no start date); next consultation by early 2027.
Governing Council decisions of January and February 2026 cover automatic remuneration of excess liquidity in TIPS accounts and rule-based liquidity transfers to and from TIPS.

TARGET is a multiplicity of component systems, one per Eurosystem central bank, each designated under national law implementing the SFD; the Guideline (adopted 24 Feb 2022, applied from 21 Nov 2022) repealed ECB/2012/27.
TARGET account types: MCAs, RTGS DCAs and sub-accounts, RTGS AS technical accounts, TIPS AS technical accounts, AS guarantee fund accounts, T2S DCAs and TIPS DCAs.
A TIPS instant payment order is deemed entered and irrevocable once funds are reserved on the participant's TIPS DCA or TIPS AS technical account (Annex I Part I Art 18(1)(b) as reported).

TIPS AS technical accounts are limited to SCT Inst or near-instant payments in the AS's books; applicants must have given the EPC a letter of intent to be an SCT Inst compliant CSM; overnight balances remunerated at the deposit facility rate.

TIPS settles instant payments in central bank money 24/7/365, final and irrevocable, compliant with SCT Inst and Nordic NCT Inst, in EUR, SEK and DKK; Norway preparing to join and Iceland interested (no dates); processes in under 100 ms.
TIPS fee is EUR 0.002 per transaction split equally between sender and receiver, plus monthly account fees, full cost recovery and no entry fee.
Eligible PSPs and ACHs open a TIPS DCA with their NCB under T2 participation rules, or are reachable parties under contract with a participant, and may delegate messaging to an instructing party.
TIPS launched in 2018, has no upper limit per transaction and processes 99.99% of payments in under five seconds; pricing applicable from 1 Jan 2024; participant list updated 1 Oct 2026.
TIPS began operations on 30 Nov 2018.

On 24 Jul 2020 the Eurosystem required SCT Inst PSPs reachable in TARGET2 to be reachable in a TIPS central bank money account and ACHs offering instant payments to move their technical accounts from TARGET2 to TIPS, targeting pan-European reach by end-2021.
The ECB states that as of 2022 SCT Inst PSPs reachable in T2 must also be reachable via TIPS.

The Eurosystem operates the technical accounts of all ancillary systems processing SCT Inst in TIPS; cover can move from TIPS accounts to AS technical accounts 24/7 (previously only during TARGET2 hours).

T2S provides DvP settlement in central bank money for 24 CSDs from 23 countries in EUR and DKK, open Monday to Friday, using ISO 20022; participants need a CSD securities account and NCB cash account.

ECMS launched 16 Jun 2025 after migration on 13 to 15 Jun as the fourth TARGET Service, replacing the national collateral systems of 20 euro-area NCBs; software by Bundesbank, Banco de Espana, Banque de France and Banca d'Italia.

ECMS manages eligible collateral for all Eurosystem credit operations, computes available credit lines, converts mobilisation instructions into T2S settlement instructions, applies harmonised collateral rules from June 2025 and uses ISO 20022.

RT1 is a real-time gross settlement system for SCT Inst with 80 participants operating around the clock; any SCT Inst PSP may join; ISO 20022; about 2 million transactions per weekday; inter-PSP processing averages just over one second (1.5 s or less).
RT1 settlement uses immediately available central bank funds in TIPS, through a dedicated TIPS cash account or across RT1 and TIPS via the AS technical account; SFD designation not stated.

EURO1 (launched 1999) is a private large-value system for single same-day euro payments described as a unique RTGS-equivalent net settlement system with immediate finality per payment; 33 participant banks; about 180,000 payments a day worth about EUR 200 billion; overseen by the ECB with Eurosystem NCBs.
STEP2-T is a pan-European ACH for mass euro payments settling in TARGET, classified by the ECB as a SIPS in August 2014, with over 4,800 PSPs and about 60 million transactions per day.
STEP2 CC provides ISO 20022-based clearing for card-initiated euro payments following the Berlin Group SEPA Card Clearing framework, based on a direct debit mechanism.

SCT Inst has been operational since November 2017 (rulebook published November 2016) and runs 24/7/365 with short pre-announced PSP maintenance windows, aiming to reach the 41 SEPA countries and territories.
SCT Inst maximum execution time: EPC page says nine seconds from receipt by the payer PSP, while the 2025 IG describes a 5-second target maximum execution time; IPR legal maximum is 10 seconds.
SCT Inst has no scheme-level maximum amount (PSPs set limits), though the EPC page meta description still says up to 15,000 euros.
EPC023-16, the binding maximum-amount document under the 2023 SCT Inst rulebook v1.2, was effective 17 Mar 2024 until 5 Oct 2025 08:00 CET.
The 2025 SCT Inst rulebook has been in effect since 5 Oct 2025 (v1.1); the 2023 rulebook v1.2 met IPR requirements from 9 Jan 2025.

2025 SCT Inst rulebook v1.2 takes effect 30 Sep 2026 with changes limited to address elements, postponing the planned 15 Nov 2026 end of unstructured addresses under all five EPC payment schemes with no new date; EPC153-22 v2.2 published alongside.
EPC122-16 IG 2025 v1.0 (issued 28 Nov 2024, published 6 Oct 2025, effective 5 Oct 2025 03:30 CET) applies to rulebook 2025 v1.1 and uses the 2019 ISO 20022 message versions.

IG dataset mapping: DS-02 pacs.008.001.08; DS-03 pacs.002.001.10; DS-05 and DS-08 camt.056.001.08; DS-06 and DS-09 pacs.004.001.09 or camt.029.001.09; DS-07 and recall status pacs.028.001.03; AccptncDtTm mandatory with milliseconds.
The IG text still says unstructured addresses end 15 Nov 2026, superseded by the rulebook v1.2 postponement.
EPC List of SEPA Scheme Countries EPC409-09 v8.0 (24 Dec 2025) lists countries and territories in scope and national non-EEA SEPA authorities; the PDF list itself was not opened.

SDD Core: no-questions refund within eight weeks of debit date, up to 13 months for unauthorised transactions; mandatory for PSPs offering euro consumer direct debits; creditor-driven mandate flow; payer PSP does not check the mandate; biller's PSP bears risk of fraudulent or erroneous collections.

SDD B2B is optional for PSPs, the payer must be a business, there is no refund for authorised transactions, it is final three business days after debit date, and the payer PSP must confirm mandate data before the first debit.

The first VOP rulebook (10 Oct 2024) covers SCT and SCT Inst with responses match, close match (with name), no match or check not possible, a target of no more than five seconds, and registration in the EPC Directory Service.

VOP rulebook v1.1 (published 16 Mar 2026), API specifications v1.1.1 and API Security Framework v2.1 are effective 20 Sep 2026; the ASF is mandatory for VOP, SRTP and SPAA participants using APIs from that date.

VOP v2.0 consultation ran 1 Apr to 30 Jun 2026, with v1.2 and v2.0 due end-November 2026; VOP is a messaging function, not a payment instrument, and cannot be relied on to identify a person or legal entity.
The IPR was published in the OJ on 19 Mar 2024; entry into force is given as 9 Apr 2024 by the Bundesbank and 8 April by the Commission page.

IPR deadlines: euro-area PSPs receive and price parity 9 Jan 2025, send and VoP 9 Oct 2025; non-euro PSPs 9 Jan 2027 and 9 Jul 2027; euro-area PIs and EMIs 9 Apr 2027; non-euro PIs and EMIs receive 9 Apr 2027, send 9 Jul 2027.

Under the IPR the payee PSP must make funds available and confirm within 10 seconds of receipt by the payer PSP (Art 5a(4)(c)); otherwise the payer PSP informs the payer free of charge and restores the account (Art 5a(4)(e), 5a(5)).
Instant transfer charges may not exceed those for other credit transfers of the corresponding type (Art 5b(1)) and VoP is free of charge (Art 5b(2)).
VoP (Art 5c) runs immediately after payee details are entered and before authorisation; a compliant PSP is not liable for misdirected funds, a non-compliant one must refund without delay (Art 5c(8)).

Art 5d: PSPs verify whether customers are subject to EU targeted financial restrictive measures at least daily and immediately after new measures, and must not screen each instant transfer for those measures; penalties of at least 10% of annual net turnover (legal persons) and at least EUR 5,000,000 (natural persons).
On request, users can set a per-day or per-transaction instant transfer limit; orders above it are not executed (Art 5a(6)).
The IPR adds PIs and EMIs to the SFD definition of institution and inserts PSD2 Art 35a requiring safeguarding, governance and wind-down arrangements, to be applied by 9 Apr 2025.
PSD2 entered into force and applied from 12 Jan 2018 per the Commission timeline, with SCA from 13 Sep 2019.

PSD2 recitals: EUR 50 payer liability for unauthorised transactions absent fraud or gross negligence; unconditional refund right for euro direct debits; max one-business-day execution; incorrect unique identifier means no PSP liability; SCA in Art 4(30) uses two or more of knowledge, possession, inherence.

PSR 2023/0210(COD) status is Awaiting Council's 1st reading position: EP first reading 23 Apr 2024, negotiation decision 21 Oct 2024, committee approval of agreed text 5 May 2026, indicative plenary 14 Dec 2026, no OJ publication.

PSD3 2023/0209(COD), repealing 2015/2366 and 2009/110, has the same stages (EP first reading 23 Apr 2024, committee approval 5 May 2026, indicative plenary 14 Dec 2026) and no final act; political agreement was reached 27 Nov 2025.

Deal contents: cash withdrawals in shops without purchase EUR 100 to 150; non-discriminatory PI access to accounts; prohibited open-banking obstacles; permissions dashboard; FRAND access to mobile device payment data; MiCA CASP route; EMIs become PIs and EMD2 is repealed; licence transition 30 months.

Hogan Lovells reports 18-month implementation (Council proposed 24) with earliest application H2 2027, and platform liability to reimbursing PSPs; FinTech Weekly says about 21 months, likely not before 2028.
FiDA 2023/0205(COD): ECON vote 18 Apr 2024, negotiation decision confirmed 18 Dec 2024, rapporteur Johan Van Overtveldt; no trilogue dates, provisional agreement or withdrawal recorded.
FiDA negotiations paused earlier in 2026, largely over large tech platforms' access; the Commission has not withdrawn it.

IFR caps consumer debit interchange at 0.2% and credit at 0.3% from 9 Dec 2015 (Art 7 from 9 Jun 2016), excluding commercial cards, cash withdrawals and three-party schemes, with Art 7 scheme/processing separation and split processing of authorisation and clearing messages.

EMD2: initial capital at least EUR 350,000, own funds at least 2% of average outstanding e-money, safeguarding under PSD rules, issuance and redemption at par, interest prohibited, transposition by 30 Apr 2011.

DORA applies from 17 Jan 2025 to 20 types of financial entities plus ICT third-party providers, covering ICT risk management, incident reporting, resilience testing incl. TLPT, third-party risk, information sharing and CTPP oversight.
GDPR document date 27 Apr 2016, entry into force 24 May 2016, repeals Directive 95/46/EC; application date (25 May 2018) not shown in fetched metadata.

AML package (AMLA Regulation 2024/1620, AMLR 2024/1624, AMLD6 2024/1640): proposal 20 Jul 2021, EP plenary 24 Apr 2024, Council adoption 30 May 2024, OJ 19 Jun 2024; the Commission labels AMLR and AMLD6 from 2027.
AMLR ELI metadata gives document date 31 May 2024 and first in-force date 10 Jul 2027.

The recast TFR (published 9 Jun 2023) applies from 30 Dec 2024 and repeals 2015/847; intra-EU transfers need only account numbers or a unique transaction identifier; crypto-asset transfers covered with no de minimis; self-hosted address assessment above EUR 1,000; five-year retention.
DGSD covers EUR 100,000 per depositor per credit institution, protects temporary high balances for 3 to 12 months, requires repayment within seven working days and a 0.8% target level by 3 Jul 2024.
EBA opinion of 10 Jun 2025 addressed PSD2 and MiCA interplay for CASPs handling e-money tokens; the No-Action Letter transition ended 2 Mar 2026.

EPI Company SE (Brussels) was authorised as a payment institution by the National Bank of Belgium on 20 Feb 2024, launched by 18 banks and financial service companies; Wero leverages SCT Inst per the page meta description.
Wero is available in Belgium, France, Germany and Luxembourg for P2P by phone number in under 10 seconds 24/7 and online shopping; in-store and subscriptions coming.

On 29 Sep 2026 Bancomat, Bizum, EPI/Wero, SIBS MB WAY and Vipps MobilePay announced a European interoperability entity; other EPI news: in-store first steps 16 Sep 2026, bunq rollout 21 Sep 2026, HiPay principal member 8 Sep 2026, nexo standards 7 Oct 2026.
EPI was announced by 16 banks on 2 Jul 2020 per the Commission timeline.

The digital euro pilot is planned for H2 2027 for 12 months with 36 euro-area PSPs selected from over 50 applicants, testing a beta version in real-life use; merchant call closes 27 Oct 2026; the page does not say whether real money is used.
Potential first digital euro issuance is 2029 assuming the Regulation is adopted in 2026; the ECB will decide on issuance only after adoption.

Digital euro phases: investigation Oct 2021 to Oct 2023, preparation Nov 2023 to Oct 2025; on 30 Oct 2025 the Governing Council moved to the next phase; 70+ entities in an innovation platform tested conditional payments.

The ECB estimates about EUR 1.3 billion development cost to first issuance (about EUR 265 million external) and about EUR 320 million a year from 2029, borne by the Eurosystem; pilot could start mid-2027 if the Regulation is adopted in 2026.

ECB FAQ (17 Aug 2026): no interest; distributed by supervised PSPs; free basic use; Eurosystem charges no scheme fees; offline details known only to payer and payee; holding limits up to EUR 3,000 tested (none set); legal tender; never programmable; centralised Eurosystem platform, not DLT.

Draft digital euro scheme rulebook v0.91 (2 Jul 2026) has annexes on testing, user journeys, end-to-end flows, front-end and back-end specs (risk and fraud, disputes, settlement, data exchange); RDG mandate 14 Jan 2026.

COM(2023) 369 (28 Jun 2023) provides legal tender with exemptions, PSP distribution with waterfall and reverse waterfall, ECB holding-limit tools and no interest, fee caps, online and offline use, no programmability, and offline privacy where ECB and NCBs get no transaction data.
The Council adopted its negotiating position on the single currency package (digital euro and euro cash legal tender) on 19 Dec 2025.

EP 2023/0212(COD): rapporteur Fernando Navarrete Rojas; ECON vote and decision to negotiate 23 Jun 2026; report A10-0185/2026 tabled 26 Jun 2026; plenary confirmed negotiations 9 Jul 2026; no provisional agreement recorded.
Votes: ECON 43-14-1; plenary 416-169-22.

Trilogues 13 Jul 2026 and 10 Sep 2026 (compensation model), with 30 Sep 2026 planned; target political agreement before end-2026 under the Irish Presidency; Parliament prefers a no-worse-off model and fee-free offline.

Third trilogue held 30 Sep 2026 with no compromise reported; Council ties fee cap to debit card charges for up to 10 years, Parliament 5 years; holding limits by Commission delegated act (Parliament) vs ECB within a Council ceiling (Council).

Freshfields: Council holding-limit ceiling by Council implementing decision on ECB recommendation, Parliament by Commission delegated act; Parliament near-ban on legal persons holding digital euro; this varies from Agence Europe's description.

Italy proposed a EUR 0.02 merchant cap for payments under EUR 10 on 8 Sep 2026 (not agreed); Parliament position that a lost device means lost offline funds; Eurogroup procedural guidance 19 Sep 2025.

Pontes was launched on 21 Sep 2026 as the Eurosystem's solution for settling tokenised assets in central bank money, listed under TARGET Services; the ECB began preparatory work to invest own funds in tokenised euro securities settled via Pontes.

Pontes connects DLT platforms with TARGET Services with a central bank money cash leg and synchronisation for DvP; at launch finality when funds movement is reflected in T2; 22.5 hours per business day; one-off onboarding fees only; 24/7 and multi-currency by mid-2028.
The Appia roadmap was published 11 Mar 2026, with a 2028 blueprint for an integrated European tokenised ecosystem including tokenised central bank money infrastructure.
2024 exploratory work (May to Nov 2024) involved 64 market participants and over 50 trials, leading to a dual-track strategy (Pontes near-term, Appia long-term).
RT1 balances are backed by central bank money on the RT1 TIPS AS technical account; precise per-participant position accounting inside RT1 is not documented in sources opened (inference).
Wero is a wallet and scheme layer, not a settlement system: value moves as commercial bank money over SCT Inst, settled via TIPS or RT1 between banks (inference).
MAS operates MEPS+, an RTGS system for large-value SGD interbank transfers.
MEPS+ SGS is the CSD and securities settlement system for scripless SGS and MAS Bills, using DvP model 1.
FAST is owned by SCHA and governed by SCHA by-laws; all FAST participants must be SCHA members.
BCS manages and operates FAST on behalf of SCHA, and BCS is owned by NETS.
PayNow is an overlay on FAST with a centralised proxy database, owned by ABS, operated by BCS and launched July 2017.
BCS, a NETS Group subsidiary, operates FAST, Interbank GIRO, eGIRO, cheque clearing, PayNow and the SGQR Central Repository (Jul 2023).

BCS is the named operator of the SGD Cheque Clearing System, USD Cheque Clearing System and Inter-bank GIRO System in S 613/2010; MAS is settlement institution for SGD cheques and GIRO; Citibank N.A. for USD cheques.
A third-party directory lists BCS as a Designated Payment System Operator regulated by MAS but disclaims accuracy and points to the MAS Financial Institutions Directory.

FAST is designated a system-wide important payment system under the PSA 2019; MAS powers over designated systems include access rules, standards, directions, inspection and approval of CEO and directors.
ABS publishes FAST and PayNow fact sheets and FAQs, the GIRO operating guidelines and the PayNow participant list; the FAST helpdesk address is FAST@bcs.sg.

SDIC insures aggregated insured deposits up to S$100,000 per depositor per Scheme member; trust and client accounts of non-bank depositors up to S$100,000 per account; CPFIS/CPFRS monies separately up to S$100,000.
SDIC is a company limited by guarantee whose board is accountable to the Minister in charge of MAS.

The deposit insurance limit rose from S$75,000 to S$100,000 effective 1 April 2024; covers SGD deposits of individuals and non-bank depositors, excludes foreign-currency deposits; members are all full banks and finance companies unless exempted by MAS.

The PDPA sets a baseline standard for personal data protection complementing sector laws such as the Banking Act; it excludes public agencies and business contact information and includes the Do Not Call Registry.
NETS ownership by DBS, OCBC and UOB is commonly stated but was not confirmed from an opened source.
MEPS+ RTGS weekday hours were 9:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m. excluding public holidays, with 63 participants as of Dec 2017 (MAS, 59 banks, CLS, CDP, SGX-DC) and SWIFT connectivity (IMF 2019).
MEPS+ settlement is immediate and irrevocable when funds suffice, otherwise queued with gridlock resolution every half hour; unsettled payments are cancelled at end of day.
SACH prepares net settlement files for SGD cheques, Inter-Bank GIRO and FAST and sends them to MEPS+ IFT for settlement within MEPS+ hours.
MAS Intraday Liquidity Facility provides interest-free intraday SGD against SGS and MAS Bills collateral (haircuts, daily mark-to-market) to participants with a GMRA executed with MAS.

MEPS+ is designated under the FNA, giving settlement finality and zero-hour-rule protection; the IMF found MEPS+ observed 17 of 18 applicable PFMI principles, broadly observing Principle 17 (operational risk).
The FNA designation order for the New MAS Electronic Payment and Book-Entry System (S 652/2006) was made 30 Nov 2006 and in operation 9 Dec 2006.

MAS and Swift published a joint ISO 20022 adoption report covering MEPS+ and next-generation SCRIPS: migration in two phases (Like-for-Like++ then Full ISO), MEPS+ messages aligned to CBPR+ and HVPS+, mapped to over 100 ISO 20022 messages.
MAS publishes current-account terms and conditions for a specified institution dated 21 July 2025 (title seen in search, not opened).
Whether MPIs hold MAS settlement accounts for FAST (suggested by the specified-institution current-account terms) is not confirmed.

FAST launched 17 March 2014 with banks; NFIs were added 8 February 2021; it runs 24x7x365; S$200,000 per transaction subject to each institution's limits; domestic only; account number required, name for reference only.
Some banks may value-date FAST transfers to the next business day after cut-off or on non-business days.
NFIs provide FAST via e-wallet accounts; e-wallet customers cannot cash out funds sourced from unsecured Singapore-issued credit card facilities.

FAST participants as of 7 Jul 2026: 32 banks and 7 NFIs (GPay Network, Liquid Group, MatchMove Pay, NIUM, SingCash, Wise Asia-Pacific, Xfers), 39 total; Hong Leong Finance listed effective 27 Aug 2026.

FAST clears instantly via SACH with deferred net settlement in two cycles per business day in MEPS+ (plans to increase cycles); participants deposit collateral with MAS covering net outflow, including for NFIs they settle for, or cannot transact further.
FAST uses ISO 20022 between participants and the ACH; an API gateway for NFIs launched Nov 2020; speed is real time (under 15 seconds).
FAST averaged over 12.5 million transactions per month in July to September 2020.
MAS announced on 30 Nov 2020 that licensed MPIs would get direct access to FAST and PayNow from Feb 2021 via an API gateway built by the Direct FAST Working Group with SCHA and ABS guidance.
FAST is designated under the FNA by the Fast and Secure Transfers Order 2021, S 82/2021.
FAST erroneous transactions are handled under the MAS E-Payments User Protection Guidelines; inter-participant disputes are handled bilaterally.
MAS Notice PSN05 sets maximum unscheduled downtime of 4 hours per 12 months for critical systems, RTO of 4 hours, 1-hour incident notification and 14-day root cause analysis.
MAS Notice PSN03 requires suspicious activity reporting within 5 working days.
The two-cycle FAST settlement figure dates from 2020/2021; the number of cycles in 2026 is unverified.
Whether NFIs settle directly in MEPS+ or through a settlement bank is unclear; the World Bank wording implies at least some settle through a participant.

PayNow sends SGD between bank or e-wallet accounts through FAST using only the recipient proxy; near-instant, 24/7/365, free for retail; proxies checked against account-opening information; sender sees recipient display name before confirming; both sides notified.
The PayNow VPA format is +(country code)(mobile number)#(MPI unique participant identifier), letting an individual link a mobile number to an MPI e-wallet while keeping a bank-linked registration.
PayNow Corporate was announced 20 Jun 2018 and launched 13 Aug 2018 for entities using UEN.
Entities may not surcharge consumers for PayNow (merchant surcharge prohibition FAQ dated 5 Jun 2026).
The PayNow nickname feature ceases from 6 Jun 2026 to counter impersonation scams.
PayNow QR adopted SGQR specifications (11 Nov 2019); 23 banks and 6 MPIs are listed as PayNow participants.
After nickname removal, masked real names are displayed (secondary, citing CNA 29 Apr and 10 Jun 2026).
PayNow registrations as of Nov 2020: 2.62 million mobile numbers, 1.8 million NRIC/FIN, over 236,000 UENs; PayNow was almost half of FAST transactions; users may register up to two accounts.
The joint MAS and ABS PayNow Gen2 study (25 Jun 2026) consulted 37 organisations across four themes.

Gen2 priority items: PayNow and NETS QR interoperability pilot by end-2026; PayNow QR deeplinking for online checkout within a year; sandboxed larger-value public-sector PayNow pilot starting next year; implementation roadmap by end-2026.
Longer-term Gen2 candidates include request-to-pay, structured data, a micropayments rail, cross-border connectivity, offline payments and agentic commerce.
The Gen2 release names 11 benchmarked jurisdictions but lists 10.

GIRO was set up in 1984 as an electronic direct debit mechanism; it is tripartite (billing organisation, customer, bank); the DDA is a contract between consumer and billing organisation; some public fees can only be paid by GIRO.
ABS Guidelines on Operating a GIRO govern roles and disputes.
eGIRO sets up GIRO deductions online, cutting set-up time from about 3 weeks to minutes; ABS and 8 banks collaborated; participating banks list dated 9 Jun 2026.
Interbank GIRO takes up to 3 working days and cheques up to 2 working days.
Larger government payments currently use GIRO with pre-registration, taking up to three business days.

S 613/2010 designates SGD Cheque Clearing, USD Cheque Clearing, Inter-bank GIRO (BCS operator) and the USD Cheque Settlement System (Citibank operator); made 21 Oct 2010, in operation 27 Oct 2010; amended by S 374/2018 from 6 Jun 2018.

SGQR+ lets merchants accept multiple schemes via one acquirer; PoC 1 to 30 Nov 2023 at over 1,000 acceptance points; islandwide rollout to about 24,000 acceptance points (over 35,000 with hawker extension).
SGQR+ technical live for existing issuers by Q4 2024 and dtcpay and MariBank by Q2 2025; cross-border SGQR supports China, Indonesia, Malaysia and Thailand.
As of June 2026 PayNow and NETS are separate QR schemes; not all bank apps can scan NETS QR and the NETS app cannot scan PayNow QR; an interoperability pilot is targeted by end-2026.
SGQR was introduced by MAS in 2018 as a single label consolidating payment QR codes; exact launch date (commonly Sept 2018) not sourced.
The PayNow and PromptPay linkage was completed (ABS release 29 Apr 2021).
PayNow and UPI participants are DBS and LiquidPay.
PayNow and DuitNow participants are Maybank, OCBC, UOB and LiquidPay.
MAS and RBI launched PayNow and UPI in Feb 2023 on cloud infrastructure; BCS caps transactions to Thailand or India at SGD 1,000 per day (Jul 2023).

Nexus started in 2022 at the BISIH Singapore Centre; in July 2024 it completed scheme, governance, commercial model and blueprint; in 2025 the central banks of India, Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Singapore and Thailand incorporated NGP for live implementation and the BIS handed over the project (page updated 27 Aug 2025).

A secondary source says Bank Indonesia was special observer until Feb 2026 when it became a full member and that go-live was expected by 2026, conflicting with BIS listing Indonesia as an NGP founder in 2025.
NGP go-live status and Singapore connection as of 15 Oct 2026 are not verified.

The PSA regulates seven payment services: account issuance, domestic money transfer, cross-border money transfer, merchant acquisition, e-money issuance, digital payment token and money-changing; licences are granted under s 6; designated payment system defined by reference to s 42; 2020 Revised Edition in operation 31 Dec 2021.
SPI thresholds: S$3m average monthly transactions for one service, S$6m for two or more, S$5m average daily e-money float; SPI base capital S$100,000 (secondary, c. 2024).
MPI base capital S$250,000 and security deposit S$100,000 or S$200,000 (secondary, c. 2024).

PSA s 23 safeguarding applies to MPIs; methods are an undertaking by a safeguarding institution to be fully liable, a guarantee for the full amount, a trust account deposit, or another prescribed method; for transfer and acquiring services relevant money is that held at end of business day, safeguarded by the next business day; for e-money, from receipt.
AML/CFT notices are PSN01 (specified payment services) and PSN02 (DPT service); technology notices PSN05 (TRM) and PSN06 (cyber hygiene); FNA-N01 covers rules of designated systems.
MAS has consulted on legislative amendments for a Single-Currency Stablecoin framework covering reserves, capital, par redemption, disclosure and recognition of foreign stablecoins.
The MAS-SCS consultation was published 1 Sep 2026 and closes 16 Oct 2026 (secondary).
The SRF and updated E-Payments Guidelines took effect 16 Dec 2024; the SRF covers seemingly authorised transactions from digital phishing impersonating legitimate entities and excludes malware.

SRF FI duties include a 12-hour cooling-off after token activation or new-device login, real-time alerts, a self-service kill switch and real-time fraud surveillance with a 24-hour hold for rapid drains (six-month transition, effective 16 Jun 2025); telco duties cover Sender ID and SMS URL filtering; loss waterfall is FI, then telco, then account holder.
A separate MAS Anti-Scam Circular applies to MPI e-wallets.

On 13 Nov 2025 MAS announced the first live issuance of SGD wholesale CBDC and settlement of interbank overnight lending among DBS, OCBC and UOB on the SGD Testnet, recorded in the banks' official books and regulatory filings.

The SGD Testnet is an operational shared-ledger infrastructure for FIs to test settlement of tokenised assets with wholesale CBDC, with common settlement asset (issue, transfer, redeem), programmability (conditional logic on counterparty payment agreements) and multi-asset atomic settlement.
Next step announced: a trial issuing tokenised MAS Bills to Primary Dealers settled in CBDC, details in 2026.
Plans for the wholesale CBDC trial were first announced on 4 Nov 2024 (secondary).

In a 9 Oct 2026 keynote at INSEAD, MAS MD Chia Der Jiun said wholesale SGD CBDC has been available through the SGD Testnet operational in 2025, that the next step is to settle tokenised MAS Bills, and that preparations can be made for issuance and use of CBDCs.
The keynote said deposit tokens hold par via exchangeability for reserves while stablecoins lack that anchor.
The keynote referenced the SAFR white paper v1.1 for agentic finance.
Chia said CBDCs will ultimately be needed to anchor monetary stability (secondary).

BLOOM (17 Oct 2025) concerns settlement using tokenised bank liabilities and well-regulated stablecoins in G10 and Asian currencies, domestic and cross-border, with tracks for distribution and clearing (Circle, DBS, OCBC, Partior, Stripe, UOB), programmable compliance (Ant International, StraitsX) and agentic payments (Coinbase, DBS).
BLOOM builds on Project Orchid (2021, more than 10 trials).
Project Guardian is MAS's industry collaboration on tokenisation and has produced shared standards.
Project Ubin phase 1 (completed March 2017) tested central-bank-issued digital tokens for domestic interbank payments.
The trial counts as live (real books) but runs on a test network, so it is labelled pilot, not production.

The PRB replaced the BPSS from 9 May 2025 under amended s.3 PSS Act; DFS gazette notification dated 6 May 2025; chaired by the RBI Governor with members DG and ED in charge of payments, Secretary DFS, Secretary MeitY and Smt. Aruna Sundararajan; RBI Principal Legal Adviser is permanent invitee under PRB Regulations 2025.
The PRB held its first meeting on 5 January 2026 in Mumbai.

NPCI is an initiative of RBI and IBA under the PSS Act, a not-for-profit company (s.25 Companies Act 1956, now s.8 of 2013 Act), with ten core promoter banks; shareholding broadened to 56 banks in 2016 and to other RBI-regulated entities in 2020.
NPCI products: RuPay, IMPS, NACH, APBS, AePS, BHIM Aadhaar, NFS, UPI, Bharat Bill Payment System, NETC/FASTag.

RBI inspected 90 PSOs in 2025-26 including 1 CCIL, 1 retail payment organisation (NPCI incl. NBBL, RuPay Cards, NBSL and NIPL), 36 non-bank PPI issuers, 30 PAs, 10 BBPOUs, 4 card networks, 4 WLAOs, 3 TReDS and 1 ATM network.

More than 11,000 circulars were consolidated as-is into 244 Master Directions for 11 types of regulated entity and about 30 functional areas; 9,445 circulars repealed; final MDs released 28 November 2025 after 770+ public comments; a Regulatory Review Cell began reviewing MDs from the quarter ended March 2026.

Commercial bank MDs dated 28 Nov 2025 include KYC (13141, updated 1 Oct 2026), Outsourcing (13139), Responsible Business Conduct (13140), Credit Information Reporting (13154, updated 1 Jul 2026), Credit and Debit Cards (13155), Credit Facilities (13156), Interest Rate on Deposits (13157), Digital Banking Channels Authorisation (13163) and Governance (13161); parallel sets exist for SFBs, payments banks, LABs, RRBs, UCBs and rural co-operative banks.
Internal Ombudsman Directions 2026 dated 14 Jan 2026 apply to commercial banks, SFBs, payments banks, NBFCs, non-bank PPI issuers and CICs.
CICs are regulated by RBI Department of Regulation and supervised by Department of Supervision; 2 MDs apply after consolidation; no penalties on CICs in 2025-26.

FIU-IND was set up by Government O.M. dated 18 November 2004 as the central national agency receiving, analysing and disseminating information on suspect financial transactions; reporting entities register and file on FINnet 2.0.
FIU-IND signed MoUs with RBI (17 April 2025) and I4C (10 April 2026); dates are from file names.
UIDAI's authentication model connects AUAs, ASAs and the CIDR; the dashboard shows 2,632.51 crore+ e-KYC transactions (no as-of date); site last reviewed 9 Oct 2026.

CERT-In Directions of 28 April 2022 require listed incidents to be reported within 6 hours, ICT logs kept 180 days within India, clocks synced to NIC/NPL NTP, VPN/cloud/VPS subscriber records kept 5 years and a designated point of contact; effective 60 days after issue (about 27 June 2022).
ReBIT (RBI subsidiary) publishes the core API technical specifications for AA participants.
Sahamati is a member-driven not-for-profit Section 8 alliance of the AA ecosystem.
SEBI, IRDAI and PFRDA regulated entities can be FIPs/FIUs; GSTN is listed as FIP under the Department of Revenue.
NBSL full name and function and NIPL/NBBL corporate details were not confirmed (NPCI subsidiary pages blocked).
Whether the NBFC-AA 2016 MD was re-issued in the Nov 2025 consolidation needs verification: the page shows last update 6 Sep 2024 and no superseded marker.
In 2025-26 UPI processed 24,16,169 lakh transactions worth ₹314.2 lakh crore (+30% volume, +20.6% value), nearly 86% of retail payment transactions.
In September 2026 UPI processed 24.07 billion transactions worth ₹29.37 lakh crore, about 802 million per day (secondary citing NPCI data).
August 2026 UPI app volume shares: PhonePe 45.64%, Google Pay 32.26%, Paytm 8.03% (secondary).
The RBI Governor cited about 490 million unique UPI users and nearly 20 billion transactions a month (Oct 2025).
NPCI circular index lists OC No. 197, FY 24-25: Implementation of 10 settlement cycles and revised business day cutover.
From 3 Nov 2025 the existing 10 UPI cycles carry only authorised transactions and disputes move to two new dedicated cycles; cycle timings not visible (secondary of NPCI circular).
